title: Mitosis and meiosis from the same parent cell
caption: Both start after S phase. Mitosis is one division and gives two diploid cells identical to the parent. Meiosis is two divisions and gives four haploid cells; with a crossover (a two-coloured chromosome) they differ from each other and from the parent.
alt: A parent cell with four chromosomes, two maternal and two paternal, each copied. Mitosis gives two cells with all four chromosomes; meiosis gives four cells with two chromosomes each, one with a chromosome that has crossed over.
description: The parent has 2n = 4 chromosomes, two from each parent, each copied in S phase.
Mitosis: one division, two cells, each 2n = 4 and identical to the parent.
Meiosis: two divisions, four cells, each n = 2, with one chromosome of each homologous pair.
A crossover swaps ends between homologues, so the four meiotic products all differ from each other and from the parent.
